messages:
sarah: Heads-up — I'm opening a small experiment thread for a KV-cache memory/regression harness. Goal: catch long-context memory growth, fragmentation, and reuse regressions in CI.

ben: Nice. Scope? synthetic workloads only or reproducible real traces?

sarah: Start synthetic (deterministic), then add a couple trimmed real traces from convo-sim. Synthetic lets us stress specific eviction+reuse patterns.

eli: Agreed. We should cover: heavy prefix reuse, random interleaving (to exercise fragmentation), and steady append-only long context (to see growth). Also a churn test where many short contexts get evicted/reauthored.

mike: For the harness I imagine: run N sequences, each with M tokens, track mem_after_token, page_alloc_count, eviction_count, reuse_hit_rate. Emit a tiny csv per run.

perf-bot: sample-run: commit 9a1c2d — kvbench v0.3 — model: rwd-30b-quantized — seqs: 10k, avg_ctx: 64k — peak_rss_mb: 4678 — final_rss_mb: 4689 — noted +11MB (0.23% over baseline).

ben: Good to have perf-bot picks up runs. We need thresholds. Proposal: fail CI if mem growth > 1% over baseline or > 50MB per 100k tokens for steady append test. Thoughts?

eli: 1% might be too strict across model variants and quant levels. Use relative thresholds per model-profile + an absolute guard. e.g., fail if >3% AND >75MB. That prevents noisy flakes.

sarah: agreed. We'll store baselines per model/quant/instance type. CI job picks correct baseline by model tag.

diana: How do we measure fragmentation+reuse concretely? Need a metric beyond RSS.

mike: Proposed metrics:
- page_count_live (num pages still mapped)
- fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_block / total_free_bytes)
- reuse_hit = kv_hits / kv_lookups (prefetch+cache hits)
- eviction_pressure = evictions_per_10k_tokens

sarah: nice. Add kv_internal_alloc_count to see small-object churn. Also record max_contiguous_kv_block_bytes (help detect fragmentation).

ben: Can we expose those via the existing /debug/kvstats endpoint? If not, add lightweight counters instrumented in the runtime. Must be cheap in perf runs.

eli: we can expose them as an opt-in sampling mode. For CI/regtest runs we enable sampling=true in runtime config. That avoids perf impact on prod.

mike: Config snippet we'll use in the harness:
```
{
  "model": "rwd-30b-quant",
  "workload": "kv_memory_reuse",
  "seq_count": 20000,
  "avg_seq_len": 120000,
  "sampling": true,
  "page_size": 65536,
  "eviction_policy": "lru",
  "report_interval_tokens": 10000
}
```

diana: For regression detection, also track time-series of rss over tokens. A steady slope indicates leak; spikes with stable baseline indicate fragmentation. Visual diffs help.

sarah: CI integration plan: nightly kvcache-memory job + PR gate for any changes touching runtime/kv or allocator. Job runs small matrix: [model-profiles: rwd-7b, rwd-13b, rwd-30b-quant], [instance: g4dn.x8, p4d-small]. Compare to saved baseline and upload csv + flamegraph to artifact store.

perf-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/kvcache/1769500000/summary.csv, flame: s3://.../flame.svg

ben: Who owns baseline maintenance? We'll need a signal when we intentionally change allocation strategy (e.g., switch page size) to update baselines.

eli: Product/eng-proc: PR that intentionally changes allocator must include a kvcache-change tag and a new baseline csv attached. CI will accept the change only if the PR includes updated baselines and a perf rationale.

mike: Also add automated regression triage: if memory growth > threshold, run a debug build with --mem-trace and collect stack traces for top alloc sites. That makes bisecting more practical.

sarah: Implementation tasks: 1) add sampling counters + /debug/kvstats hook (diana + mike) 2) harness runner + workloads (sarah + ben) 3) CI job + artifact uploader (eli) 4) PR gating docs + threshold table (sarah)

diana: I'll start instrumenting fragmentation_ratio and max_contiguous_block. Will try to keep sampling overhead <2%.

ben: I'll prototype the steady-append workload and a reuse-heavy workload (prefix reuse 80% with 1:10 churn).

eli: I'll set up a minimal airflow DAG to kick nightly runs and keep last 30 baselines. Also wire perf-bot to post summary to the thread.

sarah: timeline: prototype in this sprint, CI job + gate next sprint. If we find regressions, we'll have an emergency template for triage.

mike: One more ask: include per-token latency buckets so we can correlate memory churn with tail latency anomalies.

sarah: noted. I'll add p50/p95/p99 histograms to the csv.

perf-bot: next scheduled run queued: 1769580000 (nightly).

ben: thanks everyone — will push initial harness branch later today and tag folks in the PR. :thumbsup:
